question:
In a Compton scattering experiment, an X-ray photon of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a free electron initially at rest. After collision, the photon is scattered through an angle $\theta$ and the electron recoils.

(a) Using the photon relations for energy and momentum, explain why the photon’s speed in vacuum cannot decrease below $c$ even though it loses energy in the collision.

(b) Hence, deduce which photon property must change to account for the lost energy.

(c) For an incident wavelength $\lambda=0.10\,\text{nm}$ and scattering angle $\theta=90^{\circ}$, use the Compton shift relation

$\Delta\lambda=\lambda'-\lambda=\lambda_C(1-\cos\theta)$, where $\lambda_C=2.43\times 10^{-12}\,\text{m}$,

to calculate the scattered wavelength $\lambda'$ and comment on the change in frequency.

options.A: The speed of the photon decreases ($v < c$) after losing energy
options.B: The photon’s mass decreases to account for the energy loss
options.C: The photon’s frequency decreases (wavelength increases) while its speed remains $c$
options.D: Only the amplitude decreases; frequency and speed remain unchanged
